title: A fixed 66.83-day GJ 581 wave reduces later HARPS fit error and increases CARMENES fit error
abstract: We test a known long-period signal in GJ 581. We fit four sine waves to 125 early HARPS visits. We then fix one wave and refit the other waves in test data. The early long period is 66.82760 days. This fixed wave changes later HARPS weighted squared error by a reduction of 28.3 percent. A 90-day block range is 9.8 to 40.1 percent. A wave fitted to all 250 HARPS visits increases error by 46.4 percent in 54 CARMENES visits, with a reduction-score range of -104.4 to 3.4 percent. Nearby periods with similar early fit errors can reverse the later HARPS score. These tests concern a known signal and do not establish a planet or a cause. Ranges hold the periods fixed and omit period selection error. The package contains raw inputs, source hashes, code, controls, figures, and offline steps.

display.caption: Fixed-wave prediction scores and conditional 90-day block ranges. Positive scores reduce test error. Other wave coefficients are fitted in test data.
Long-period sensitivity. The upper panel uses only early HARPS. The lower panel evaluates prediction without selecting a period from test data.
